question: Would a dual-oracle trigger actually reduce basis risk for a maize index?
What happens if an n8n workflow becomes an agent instead of a flowchart?
Can a till receipt tell you more about a small business than its bank statement?
How cheap can a meeting-to-actions pipeline actually get?
Is vector search worth it for a corpus of 400 documents?
Can a QR code replace the registration desk at a campus event?
Can I automate the thing I do every Sunday night?
Does an SMS fallback actually change collection rates?
What does a payment look like if you draw every state it can be in?
note: Hypothesis: requiring agreement between a weather oracle (CHIRPS anomaly + NDVI time-series) and a yield oracle (crop-health classification) cuts false positives. What I do not know yet is the conflict policy — when the two disagree, does human review scale, or does it just move the cost from field visits to desk review?

Rebuilt a fixed six-step ops workflow as a tool-calling loop.
 It handled the edge cases the flowchart couldn't and invented two failure modes the flowchart never had. Kept the tools, threw away the autonomy.
Parsed a month of M-Pesa till confirmations into a daily revenue series. The shape of a week is extremely legible — Fridays, month-end, school terms. Formal statements flatten all of that out.
Upload, transcribe, diarise, summarise, extract commitments. Works. The transcription cost per hour is the whole business model, and at Kenyan price points it doesn't close yet.

Stood up Milvus, embedded everything, built the retrieval layer. Then tested it against Postgres full-text search. At this size, full-text won on latency and lost almost nothing on relevance. Deleted the cluster.
Built for a Chiromo Tech Club event. It worked at the desk and failed in the queue — nobody has signal in the corridor. Now caches locally and syncs after.

A scheduled job that pulls the week's payment events, diffs them against expected rent and posts a single summary. Ninety minutes of work replaced by a message. The prototype for how I now think about all internal tooling.
Africa's Talking behind the reminder system, for tenants who never open the app. Too small a sample to claim a number, but the qualitative answer is yes — the channel matters more than the message.
Not code. A wall of paper. Pending, pushed, timed-out, partial, duplicated, reversed, orphaned, reconciled. Nineteen states. This drawing is why the LEA ledger got rewritten.
